messages:
Matt H.: quick heads-up — I'm seeing a couple of related Go CVEs in our dependency tree: grpc has an auth header parsing issue around v1.50.x, and the oauth/jwt helper lib we vendor appears to have a token validation edge-case. Can we do a quick triage?
Priya S.: thanks. do you have the CVE ids and affected ranges?
Matt H.: CVE-2026-1212 for grpc (affects 1.49.0 -> 1.50.3), CVE-2026-1220 for go-jwt-helper (<= v0.9.1). net/http is flagged by a fuzz report but looks low impact for our usages — link: https://oss-db.example/CVE-2026-1212
Olivia R.: are these exploitable in hosted or only in local tooling?
Matt H.: grpc issue can be triggered by crafted auth headers over inbound server streams — could affect our public hosted endpoints if a model runtime accepts external client tokens. go-jwt-helper is more about signature validation edge cases when JWK rotation is concurrent.
Sasha G.: ok risk note: hosted API + Dedicated ingress are in scope. Private deployments are customer-managed but worth notifying.
Priya S.: proposed mitigations? pin versions, backport patches, or temporary WAF rule to strip suspicious headers?
Matt H.: plan: 1) immediate: add minimal go.mod pin + replace directives in affected services to force grpc v1.51.0 (patched) and go-jwt-helper v0.10.0, run full unit+integration, roll canary to staging. 2) medium: create hotpatch branch for any services that can't bump easily, build small backport (we have a cherry-pick for grpc fix in internal patch). 3) communication: security advisory + customer notice for Dedicated/Private about recommended upgrades.
Olivia R.: for the pin, please include a short playbook. Also call out MVS caveats — other transitive deps might pull older grpc.
Matt H.: playbook snippet:
```
# service repo: token-service
go get google.golang.org/grpc@v1.51.0
# or add to go.mod
replace google.golang.org/grpc => google.golang.org/grpc v1.51.0
run: go mod tidy && go test ./...
```
Matt H.: also check `go list -m all` to validate single grpc version across module graph. If downstream modules require older version, use a temporary replace in top-level monorepo.
Priya S.: how long until we can have a canary in staging?
Sasha G.: I can take the staging rollout, aiming EOD PST today if tests pass. Need approval for a short maintenance window for one service.
Matt H.: prioritization: token-service, api-gateway, and runtime-ingester are P0 (handle auth headers). Others P1.
Olivia R.: any KMS or RBAC implications? e.g., rotating keys or KMS signatures during rollout?
Matt H.: KMS unaffected by these code fixes. For jwt rotation, ensure JWKS fetch has jitter/backoff. I'll attach an eval to confirm no change to KMS usage. RBAC: no policy changes needed.
Priya S.: add a note to incident channel and create advisory doc for customers. sec-bot: can you start an automatic vuln ticket and label as P0?
sec-bot: created vuln-1945 with severity P0, assigned to @matt_h, ETA flag: 24h.
Sasha G.: I'll do the canary after Matt posts the patched images. Matt, ping when images are uploaded.
Matt H.: will do. I also recommend a short-lived header stripping WAF rule on the public LB until canary done. Ops, please weigh in.
Ops (via Ops-alert): WAF rule draft ready, can apply for 2h window.
Priya S.: great — next steps: Matt to open PRs with replace pins + tests, Sasha to canary, Ops to apply WAF if needed, Olivia to validate transitive deps. We'll update customers after canary verifies.
Matt H.: thanks all. I'll post PR links here shortly and tag the advisory doc.
